previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type II diabetes, hypertension, and depression, was admitted for severe hyperglycemia with a blood glucose of 754 mg/dL after missing her morning NPH insulin and consuming sweetened tea. She did not have diabetic ketoacidosis. Her insulin regimen was changed from NPH to glargine 32 units at bedtime with a humalog sliding scale due to poor glycemic control and prior hypoglycemia. She received nutrition counseling and education on insulin pen use. Her creatinine improved from 1.5 to 1.1 mg/dL, likely due to resolution of prerenal acute kidney injury, and she has follow-up scheduled with nephrology. Skin abscesses from a prior admission were monitored, remained clean without infection, and continued on outpatient wound care. She was discharged home with home health services, new insulin therapy, and follow-up arranged for diabetes, surgery, and kidney function.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with DMII, HTN and depression with a recent admission 
for hyperglycemia who presents with alcohol intoxication, noted 
to have an anion gap acidosis.
 
#. Anion gap acidosis: Differential included alcoholic 
ketoacidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis, also lactic acidosis 
contributing to anion gap, methanol or ethylene glycol toxicity. 
Absence of ketones in urine suspicious, however assay picks up 
urine acetoacetate and acetone, but not ß-hydroxybutyrate. No 
serum ketones sent. UA and CXR not concerning for infection. 
Reports missing a few doses of glargine in days PTA. Patient 
initially placed on insulin drip, then home insulin retarted 
once anion gap closed and patient began taking po's.  Lactate 
trended down 0.8.  

#. Alcohol intoxication: H/o alcohol abuse. Serum EtOH over 400 
at presentation, about 8 hours prior to ICU arrival. Patient was 
placed on CIWA scale for withdrawal symptoms.  Social work was 
consulted. She was given thiamine and folate.

#. DMII: Poorly controlled, limited outpatient follow-up 
documented in OMR. Recent A1C was 12.7. She has had 2 prior 
episodes of DKA in the record, both occurring in the setting of 
d/c'ed insulin use at home. ___ was consulted and recommended 
lowering lantus dose to 20u daily, given concern for am 
hypoglycemia. On discharge they also recommended starting 
glimepiride 2mg daily in lieu of a sliding scale since the 
patient has not been able to adhere to a sliding scale regimen.

#. Depression: History of depression, with one psych 
hospitalization in ___ for SI, though no current suicidality.  
Patient was continued on home paroxetine

#. Transitional issues:

infection. Will need to have this followed up. Consider HIV
